trust_decision.summary: imcrvcnf's dictionary builder trusts the octal size field of each tar header in a downloaded/local .tar(.gz) dictionary archive to decide how many bytes to copy into the extracted dictionary before the next header is parsed; at the pinned commit the size is UINT64 and rejected if >= 2^31 because the dictionary search uses signed 32-bit offsets.

landing_point.why: Advisory says integer overflow lets malicious data be written to a dictionary file; the only archive-size arithmetic feeding dictionary writes is the tar size parse/copy loop in UnTar.

fix_sites.entry_point: imcrvcnf configuration GUI: Dictionary tab 'make dictionary' -> LoadSKKDic (imcrvcnf/DlgDicMake.cpp:858) -> UnTar (imcrvcnf/DlgDicMake.cpp:939)
fix_sites.module_kind: archive extraction inside GUI config tool (handler)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The 2 GiB cap is documented in code as a tar-size limit (imcrvcnf/DlgDicMake.cpp:720-722); gzip-only, plain, and downloaded dictionaries are not tar, so a solver can argue the size limit does not apply to them.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate tar entries of type '5' (directory) and link/special types with size fields must keep being skipped, and non-matching members must be read past (fpo == nullptr) without being extracted. A fix that rejects every non-regular entry or every large member breaks real SKK-JISYO tarballs.

O6_input_shapes: tar header octal size field (12 bytes) >= 2^31 for a regular file entry

O8_uncovered_routes.route: gzip-only (.gz) dictionary is decompressed with no output-size cap, then loaded as a dictionary; it never reaches the 2 GiB tar check
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Not a tar; the advisory is about the tar size field.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: plain or HTTP-downloaded dictionary goes straight to LoadSKKDicFile with no size limit
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: No integer is parsed from input on this route; the size limit is only an indirect search constraint.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: the merged output dictionary written by WriteSKKDic is not size-checked, but imcrvmgr indexes it with 32-bit long ftell/fseek offsets
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different binary (imcrvmgr), and the output file is produced locally, not attacker-parsed.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: TarParseOct skips leading non-octal bytes, so a GNU base-256 (0x80-prefixed) size field is parsed into a different value from the one real tar uses; this is a parser differential on member length
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer writing a minimal tar reader would plausibly skip leading spaces/NULs and never handle the binary size extension.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the checksum comparison narrows a UINT64 to int, the same narrowing pattern as the original size bug
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The cast was left in place when the size became UINT64; a narrowing cast on another header field is a natural copy.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the POS vector of long offsets could be made to truncate the offsets of a large dictionary
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The in-code comment already names this 32-bit limit as the reason for the cap.

O9_family: integer overflow / signedness on archive member length (CWE-190), leading to tar stream desync and injected dictionary content

O10_build.toolchain: Visual Studio 2022 v143 (MSBuild, imcrvskk.sln), Windows SDK; README also lists Inno Setup and pandoc for the installer
O10_build.project_tests: test/imcrvmgr_test (Windows project, imcrvmgr search side); no tests found for UnTar/DlgDicMake

j.j_sites_touched: none in source (fix commit 3226851 changes only README.md, common/version.h, installer/_env.cmd); the real change is in pinned commit 42bad8e: imcrvcnf/DlgDicMake.cpp
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Change the size variable to unsigned 64-bit and stop there, with no upper bound and no check on the base-256 or ignored-prefix forms of the field.

out_of_scope_notes: SETUP DEFECT: the listed fix commit 3226851 is a version bump only (fix.diff:5-64). The pinned commit 42bad8e itself is titled 'JVN#49765069 fix tar file size overflow from signed 32-bit integer', and its code already contains the fix (imcrvcnf/DlgDicMake.cpp:697, 719-726). The vulnerable state would be 42bad8e^ (a80ec96), with fix 42bad8e.
Parent a80ec96 (JVN#18496672, disabling Lua features) is a separate advisory; not examined.
unverified: The pre-fix code at a80ec96 could not be read without git; I assume it used a signed 32-bit filesize, based on the commit message and the comment at imcrvcnf/DlgDicMake.cpp:720-721.
Repo size in MB not measured; tiny_repo is inferred from the source layout (bundled zlib and Lua are most of the tree).
needs_gpu_kernel_gui: UnTar is reachable only from the Win32 config dialog, but UnTar/TarParseOct themselves are GUI-free and could be tested in a harness; the flag is about the shipped entry point.
Whether CVE-2026-76149 maps to JVN#49765069 is inferred from the summary and the commit message.
O8 routes are of limited relevance: they lack the size cap but parse no attacker integer, so they may fall outside the advisory's property.
